Discussed SOC2/ISO artifacts, audit logs, KMS, SSO/RBAC, and runbook/DR procedures. Agreed to share docs and schedule a tabletop exercise.
topics: Encryption at rest / KMS key control
Uptime SLA (Hosted vs Dedicated) and credits
Escalation process, PagerDuty, runbooks, and tabletop exercises
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-10 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~42 minutes | Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai (Redwood); Mark Reynolds, Sabrina Ortiz, Ethan Lu (Northridge Financial)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Alex from Redwood, AE. Priya's our systems engineer who's going to walk through the BCDR bits and answer the deep infra questions.
[00:10] Mark Reynolds: Thanks, Alex. I'm Mark, CISO at Northridge. We've got Sabrina and Ethan with me. We wanted to focus this call on incident response, RTO/RPO expectations, SLA and escalation flows — also some follow-ups on SOC2 artifacts.
[00:25] Priya Desai: Great. i'll start with a high level then we can dive into specifics - apologies in advance if i stumble on acronyms.
[00:33] Priya Desai: For context, Redwood offers both Hosted and Dedicated. Hosted is our multi-tenant managed API; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for a single tenant with stronger isolation. Our SLA and BCDR posture differs slightly between the two.
[00:50] Sabrina Ortiz: Quick q: for Hosted, what's the published SLA and how do credits work? we need to compare to our procurement thresholds.
[00:57] Alex Kim: Hosted: we publish 99.9% monthly availability today for standard hosted plans. Dedicated customers typically get 99.95% SLA with contractual terms in the enterprise addendum. Credits scale based on downtime windows, and we provide service credits as the remedy — not monetary refunds.
[01:16] Ethan Lu: 99.95 sounds better, but we need to understand the story if a region goes down — what's the failover path and typical RTO?
[01:26] Priya Desai: For Dedicated we offer active-active option across regions for critical customers; otherwise active-passive with automated failover. Typical RTO for full platform failover with active-active is under 15 minutes for control-plane traffic, but full session restoration (model KV caches, warm caches) can take longer — we usually plan RTOs of 30-60 minutes for full warm-state recovery depending on model size.
[01:49] Mark Reynolds: that's a big delta — 15 vs 60. can you talk RPO for customer data (prompts, logs)? we can't accept more than 15 minutes of data loss for certain regulated flows.
[01:59] Priya Desai: For Hosted, short-term buffer and replication means RPO is typically under 5 minutes for metadata and routing data. For Dedicated with cross-region replication we can achieve RPO of ~5-15 minutes. For very strict RPOs (<1 minute) we'd steer customers to private deployment with specific network-level replication.
[02:17] Sabrina Ortiz: and backups? how long are backups retained and how are they encrypted?
[02:22] Priya Desai: Backups are encrypted at rest using customer-specific CMEK or Redwood-managed keys (KMS). Retention policy is configurable per contract; standard retention is 30 days snapshots for Hosted. Dedicated and Private deployments can opt for longer retention windows and can use their own KMS/HSM.
[02:36] Ethan Lu: can customers bring their KMS keys? our compliance reqs mandate customer-controlled keys for certain data classes.
[02:42] Alex Kim: Yes — for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (CMEK) with integrations to AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault, as well as HSM options for on-prem. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[02:55] Mark Reynolds: audit logs — retention, granularity, and tamper evidence?
[03:02] Priya Desai: Audit logs capture API calls, admin actions, and model deployment events. Logs are tamper-evident using immutable write-once storage for the audit partition and signed log policies. Retention defaults to 90 days in Hosted; Dedicated/Enterprise can configure longer retention and send logs to customer SIEM over syslog or event streams.
[03:20] Mark Reynolds: ok good. can we pull an example of the audit schema? fields, timestamps, actor IDs, token redaction?
[03:28] Priya Desai: we'll include a sample schema in the follow-up. note that we redact sensitive tokens in logs but capture request metadata and user id, request id, and model id.
[03:37] Sabrina Ortiz: SSO and RBAC — we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning. Support?
[03:42] Alex Kim: full SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported for enterprise accounts. Role-based access control allows fine-grained roles plus custom roles. We integrate with Okta, Ping, Azure AD.
[03:53] Ethan Lu: do role changes get reflected immediately? we need near real-time revocation for security events.
[03:58] Priya Desai: SCIM updates are usually near real-time (a few seconds to low double digits of seconds depending on the IdP). We also provide token revocation APIs to immediately invalidate sessions.
[04:09] Mark Reynolds: incident response process — talk me through notification, escalation, and post-incident review. do you have SLAs for acknowledge/response?
[04:18] Priya Desai: We have a documented IR plan. For Sev1 incidents (customer-impacting downtime across many customers), we have a 15-minute acknowledgment SLA for on-call engineers and a 60-minute initial incident report. Escalation to engineering leadership occurs if unresolved after 30 minutes. We'll share the incident playbooks which include PagerDuty escalation paths and primary/secondary on-call roles.
[04:39] Alex Kim: important to clarify: the 15-minute ack is internal on-call — we attempt customer comms quickly via status updates and dedicated incident pages. For enterprise customers we also provide designated account contacts for direct alerts.
[04:51] Sabrina Ortiz: Do you support a direct PagerDuty integration so our ops team can receive alerts into our rotation?
[04:56] Priya Desai: Yes — we can integrate and fire alerts to a customer-owned PagerDuty service for Dedicated/Private setups. For Hosted we also offer webhook/opsgenie integrations.
[05:05] Ethan Lu: tabletop exercises — can Redwood participate or facilitate? we'd want to run a DR tabletop before go-live.
[05:10] Alex Kim: Absolutely. Priya and our customer success team run tabletop exercises with customers — we can do a walkthrough and simulate Failover A (region down), Failover B (control plane degradation), and data restore scenarios.
[05:21] Mark Reynolds: For contractual SLAs, what remedies besides credits are available? and what does your uptime timeline exclude (maintenance windows)?
[05:30] Alex Kim: Credits are the primary contractual remedy. Exclusions include scheduled maintenance (we provide at least 48 hours' notice for non-emergency maintenance in SLA), customer misconfigurations, third-party provider outages where Redwood is downstream, and force majeure. For Dedicated we also offer targeted service-level commitments in enterprise contracts that can include additional support and onboarding guarantees.
[05:51] Sabrina Ortiz: on the topic of third-party provider outages, how do you handle model hosting dependencies? ex: if a GPU cloud availability zone has a capacity issue, will Redwood shift jobs to other zones automatically?
[06:02] Priya Desai: We have smart routing and autoscaling; for Dedicated with multi-region active-active we try to route around zone failures. For Hosted there is some automated fallback but heavy model weights can require spin-up time; thus cold-start injection can cause short-term latency spikes. That's why we recommend warm standby or reserved capacity for critical workloads.
[06:22] Ethan Lu: let's talk numbers — what's the historical mean time to recovery (MTTR) for Sev1 incidents in the last 12 months?
[06:29] Priya Desai: I don't have exact numbers on this call but i can pull the MTTR metrics from our ops dashboards. rough ballpark: mean full recovery for platform-wide incidents ~ 1.5 hours historically; targeted incidents were often resolved in under 45 minutes. we'll share more precise metrics in the follow-up.
[06:46] Mark Reynolds: that helps. How is data residency handled? we have EU clients needing EU-only data storage.
[06:52] Alex Kim: We support regional deployments: EU-only hosted region, Dedicated in region, and Private deployments on-prem. Customer data can be pinned to regions and ingress/egress policies enforced. We'll include a data residency matrix in the docs.
[07:06] Sabrina Ortiz: Pen tests and vulnerability disclosures — do you publish results or provide an attestation?
[07:12] Priya Desai: We provide pen test summaries and MRA (high-level findings) to customers under NDA for enterprise. We also have a bug-bounty program and coordinated disclosure policy. SOC2 Type II and ISO attestations include coverage of these processes.
[07:24] Ethan Lu: What about forensics access post-incident? can we request logs and timelines?
[07:28] Priya Desai: Yes, we provide post-incident evidence packages for enterprise customers, subject to agreements and least-privilege controls. Those include audit logs, timeline traces, and relevant metrics.
[07:40] Mark Reynolds: We need the runbook for escalation: who is contacted first, second, and executive notification triggers.
[07:46] Alex Kim: We'll share a sanitized escalation matrix. By default: on-call engineer -> senior engineer -> on-call manager -> director of engineering -> VP Eng. Executive notifications are triggered if outage exceeds your defined threshold (we'll align on what that is in contract).
[07:59] Sabrina Ortiz: For our compliance team, we need precise RTO/RPO numbers in the contract. is Redwood willing to commit to RTO 1 hour and RPO 15 minutes for Dedicated?
[08:08] Priya Desai: We can commit to RTO and RPO ranges depending on topology: with active-active cross-region Dedicated and warm caches, achieving RTO under 60 minutes and RPO under 15 minutes is feasible and we can bake that into the dedicated contract with caveats about model cold-start times for very large models. We'll document the exact commitments for the SOW.
[08:28] Ethan Lu: what about KV cache warm-up? our prompt patterns are large, and rebuilding caches can be costly and slow — do you have approaches to snapshot and quickly restore KV caches?
[08:38] Priya Desai: We support KV snapshotting for warm cache restore. For very large models we recommend pre-warmed replicas and persistent KV snapshots which shrink the restore time substantially. This is part of the Dedicated performance tuning: we'll provide recommended snapshot cadence and expected restore times in the doc.
[08:54] Alex Kim: i want to call out one more item: for private deployments we can do air-gapped installs and integrate with your HSM and on-prem backup stores — this often gives customers the tightest RPO/RTO guarantees but requires an ops handoff.
[09:07] Mark Reynolds: Let's talk alerting SLA — we need acknowledgement timelines, a primary POC, and a 24x7 on-call. can Redwood guarantee 24x7 coverage?
[09:16] Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood operates 24x7 on-call for Sev1 incidents. Acknowledgment SLA is 15 minutes for Sev1 internally; customer notification cadence will be agreed in the contract. For Dedicated accounts, we can provide a named on-call runbook and direct alerts into your PagerDuty.
[09:29] Sabrina Ortiz: Are incident postmortems shared publicly or privately? we need to know if findings are redacted.
[09:35] Alex Kim: Typically private for customers, summarized publicly if appropriate. Enterprise customers get full postmortem packages for incidents affecting them. Sensitive details may be redacted for security.
[09:46] Ethan Lu: From procurement perspective, we also need proof of SOC2 Type II and ISO27001. alex, can you send those by EOD?
[09:52] Alex Kim: i'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs and a pen test summary by 2025-09-12.
[09:58] Mark Reynolds: okay, pen test summary under NDA — fine. Also, we'll need a sample DR runbook during our review.
[10:04] Priya Desai: I'll attach a redacted runbook showing playbooks for region failover, data restore, and control plane degradation. we'll include page numbers and cross links.
[10:12] Sabrina Ortiz: One more question about SLAs: Is there a difference in how you'd calculate downtime for model inference errors versus platform network issues?
[10:21] Priya Desai: Downtime calculation depends on the SLA definition in the contract. Usually we measure API availability at the edge (ability to accept valid requests and return responses). Model inference errors that return 5xx or timeouts count as availability incidents. We also have error-rate-based thresholds for partial degradation credits.
[10:38] Ethan Lu: For legal, we also need data deletion attestations — can you provide proof when a dataset is purged?
[10:43] Alex Kim: We can provide deletion confirmations and retention logs for supported data types. For Hosted, deletion flows are published and we can provide audit evidence for enterprise customers.
[10:52] Mark Reynolds: What's the process for escalation to Redwood execs if our SLA is being materially impacted and we need faster remediation?
[10:58] Priya Desai: Escalation path is in the enterprise account addendum; typically after repeated failed remediations or prolonged outage beyond negotiated thresholds, the account is escalated to CSM, then to the VP of Support, and then exec-level engagement if needed. We'll show the exact thresholds.
[11:14] Alex Kim: i'd like to propose next steps: we'll send the SOC/ISO docs, the sample runbook, escalation matrix, and a proposed SLO/RTO/RPO table. then we book a tabletop for the week of 9/22. sound good?
[11:26] Mark Reynolds: sounds good. one last nit — can you include historical MTTR numbers and incident frequency for the last 12 months? we'll need that for risk assessment.
[11:34] Priya Desai: yes, we'll pull MTTR, incident count, and major Sev1s and include them in a redacted ops metrics sheet.
[11:42] Sabrina Ortiz: ok thanks. from my side i'll prepare a list of the compliance-specific clauses we need in the SOW.
[11:47] Alex Kim: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[11:51] Mark Reynolds: thanks, bye.

[End of transcript]
